A standalone HDMI recorder is a device that records video and audio directly from an HDMI source onto an SD card, USB drive, or SSD, without needing a computer.

Typical uses include recording from cameras, gaming consoles, video players, and other HDMI devices.

The key distinction is between a true standalone recorder and a USB HDMI capture card, which requires a connected computer.

chats.answer:
A standalone HDMI recorder is a device that records video and audio directly from an HDMI source (computer, camera, game console, etc.) without needing a PC.

For true standalone recording, look for:

HDMI input — accepts video from your source.

USB drive, SD card, or SSD recording — saves footage locally.

No computer required — starts and stops recording using physical buttons.

1080p60 or 4K support — depending on your recording needs.

HDMI passthrough — optional, lets you connect a monitor while recording.

Be careful: many products advertised as HDMI capture cards require a computer and are not standalone recorders.
